P01.rationale: There is no founder portrait or dominant human anchor on this page; the only imagery consists of a factory scene and product mockups.

P05.rationale: The case study clearly features a named client (Hanisch & Klein) with their specific role listed in the right-hand column.

P07.rationale: A testimonial quote is present at the bottom of the right column, though it lacks the visual weight or grid structure of a full press wall.

P10.rationale: The page features oversized decorative typographic elements, specifically the giant '05' numeral and large percentage figures.

P11.rationale: Data visualizations are present in the form of specific metrics (e.g., '100%') and a product mockup showing an app interface, though they lack complex charts or before/after comparisons.

P12.rationale: The layout is dense and magazine-quality, utilizing a two-column structure that fills the sheet with text, graphics, and typography.

P13.rationale: An intentional background texture/atmosphere is present in the form of a subtle paper grain effect across the entire page.

P14.rationale: While there are no full-bleed photos with overlaid text on this specific page, the design demonstrates good readability principles generally.

P16.rationale: A device/product mockup is clearly shown in the top left quadrant, displaying a laptop and smartphone to add product credibility.

N07.rationale: The imagery appears specific to a real business context (factory floor) rather than generic stock photography.

N08.rationale: There is minimal dead whitespace; the layout is tightly packed with content in both columns.

N10.rationale: Text does not sit on busy photos without a scrim or awkward inset gaps; typography is placed cleanly against solid backgrounds or paper texture.
